claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this accurately, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation and any children you're claiming for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children you're claiming Child Benefit for? If so, could you tell me their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 20 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I appreciate you providing that context.

Before I can assess Alex's eligibility, I need to check the specific rules around Child Benefit. Let me look up the eligibility criteria to ensure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information I've reviewed, I can see that Child Benefit eligibility for children aged 16 or over has specific requirements. Since Alex is 20 years old, I need to ask you an important question:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

This is key because Child Benefit can normally continue until age 20 if your child stays in approved education or training, but would stop once they reach 16 if they're not in such education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school a while back and hasn't started anything else since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I now have enough information to make a determination about Alex's eligibility.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility criteria, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16, or if your child is 16 or over but stays in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 20 years old and is not currently in approved education or training, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. 

Here's why: Child Benefit can only be claimed for children under 16, or for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 20 years old and is not currently in any approved education or training, he no longer qualifies for Child Benefit.

If Alex were to enter approved education or training in the future, you may be able to claim again, but for now, unfortunately he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
